[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#ruling-statement]

## Ruling Statement

> **Material UI (MUI v5+) is not approved for new frontend development at Gainwell Technologies.**

This ruling is issued in response to team requests to adopt Material UI for React-based frontend work. The enterprise decision is established and recorded in **ADR-APP-003** (UI Component System Selection, accepted 2026-04-08). This Architecture Ruling Document (ARD) communicates and enforces that decision. It does not supersede or modify ADR-APP-003, STD-TEC-NXT-003, or STD-APP-UI-001 — it routes teams to those authoritative sources and provides the approved alternative path.

**The approved enterprise UI stack is: Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS**, per ADR-APP-003. This is the mandatory going-in default for all new React-based frontend development at Gainwell Technologies.

---
page_texts.4:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#context]

## Context

A UI development team has requested approval to use Material UI (MUI v5+) for React-based frontend work. This request conflicts with an existing enterprise decision.

**ADR-APP-003** (accepted 2026-04-08) formally adopts Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS as the enterprise standard UI component system and explicitly rejects Material UI. The Enterprise MFE Architecture CRB submission (2026-04-08) selected a custom design system built on Radix UI primitives over Material UI and Ant Design, citing branding control and healthcare-specific component requirements. **STD-TEC-NXT-003** mandates Shadcn/UI, Radix UI, and Tailwind CSS for all Next.js applications.

This ARD is the formal team-facing enforcement instrument for ADR-APP-003. Architecture Ruling Documents are issued when a team request conflicts with an existing enterprise architectural decision, to provide a clear, authoritative response that eliminates ambiguity.

---
page_texts.5:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#rejection-rationale]

## Rejection Rationale

The following technical rationale is sourced from ADR-APP-003 and GUID-APP-TEC-003. No new normative requirements are introduced here; these are summaries of the rationale already recorded in those documents.
page_texts.6:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#1-bundle-size-violates-enterprise-module-budget]

### 1. Bundle Size Violates Enterprise Module Budget

Material UI carries a **~1.2MB bundle** (source: GUID-APP-TEC-003 §Technical Context — What Was Rejected and Why). The enterprise ≤500KB gzipped per-module budget established in **ADR-APP-002** (Frontend Framework Selection) is immediately violated by importing Material UI. The CSS-in-JS Emotion runtime that MUI depends on adds further per-module overhead. Shadcn/UI components are copied into the codebase — no runtime library import, total tree-shaking — and do not contribute to the module bundle at all.
page_texts.7:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#2-css-in-js-emotion-conflicts-with-the-enterprise-design-token-strategy]

### 2. CSS-in-JS (Emotion) Conflicts with the Enterprise Design Token Strategy

Material UI's CSS-in-JS runtime (Emotion) cannot be cleanly mixed with Tailwind CSS without CSS specificity conflicts (source: ADR-APP-003 — Considered Options, Option 2; GUID-APP-TEC-003 §Principle 2). The enterprise design token strategy (GUID-APP-UI-001) relies on CSS custom properties consumed by Tailwind CSS. Emotion injects scoped styles at runtime that compete with Tailwind's utility class specificity, breaking predictable style application. Teams using MUI alongside Tailwind must maintain two parallel styling systems with no clean integration boundary.
page_texts.8:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#3-material-design-visual-language-does-not-align-with-gainwell-healthcare-branding]

### 3. Material Design Visual Language Does Not Align with Gainwell Healthcare Branding

Material UI implements Google's Material Design visual language — a consumer-focused design system that does not match Gainwell's healthcare product branding requirements (source: ADR-APP-003 — Considered Options, Option 2; GUID-APP-TEC-003 §Business Context). Gainwell serves 50+ state Medicaid agencies, each potentially requiring distinct theming. Adapting MUI's opinionated Material Design aesthetics to healthcare product UX requires learning and overriding MUI's proprietary `sx` prop and `ThemeProvider` API, rather than using standard CSS variables. The Gainwell design system is built on unstyled Radix UI primitives, re-themed per state via CSS variables with zero component logic changes.
page_texts.9:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#4-wcag-22-aa-accessibility-cannot-be-directly-fixed-by-teams]

### 4. WCAG 2.2 AA Accessibility Cannot Be Directly Fixed by Teams

Material UI's WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility compliance is dependent on MUI's upstream release cadence (source: ADR-APP-003 — Considered Options, Option 2). When an accessibility issue is found in an MUI component, engineering teams cannot fix it without forking the library. Gainwell has contractual WCAG 2.2 AA and Section 508 obligations for all state MMIS implementations. Radix UI provides accessibility-correct primitives that teams own and can remediate directly. Shadcn/UI's copy-into-codebase model gives teams full control over component source.
page_texts.10:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#5-enterprise-crb-explicitly-selected-radix-ui-over-material-ui]

### 5. Enterprise CRB Explicitly Selected Radix UI Over Material UI

The **Enterprise MFE Architecture CRB** submission (2026-04-08) explicitly selected a custom design system built on Radix UI primitives over Material UI and Ant Design, citing branding control and healthcare-specific component requirements (source: GUID-APP-TEC-003 §Strategic Alignment; Enterprise MFE Architecture CRB). This is a formal governance-body decision, not an individual team preference.

---
page_texts.11:
[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#approved-alternative]

## Approved Alternative

**Use Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS** per [ADR-APP-003](./ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md).

| Layer            | Technology          | Role                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primitives       | Radix UI            | Accessible, unstyled headless component primitives                    |
| Component layer  | Shadcn/UI           | Pre-built components using Radix UI + Tailwind CSS; copied into repo  |
| Styling          | Tailwind CSS v3+    | Utility-first CSS; design token CSS variables mapped to Tailwind config |
| Data grid        | TanStack Table v8   | Headless table/grid for standard tabular data                         |
| Complex grid     | Kendo UI for React  | Full-featured grid/chart when TanStack Table is insufficient (requires ADR) |

**Implementation guidance**: [GUID-APP-TEC-003 — UI Component System Guidance](../../strategy/guidance/application/ui-component-system/GUID-APP-TEC-003-ui-component-system-guidance.md)

Shadcn/UI components are not installed as an npm dependency. The `shadcn` CLI copies component source files directly into the repository under `src/components/ui/`. Teams own that code and can modify it for product-specific requirements while retaining the Radix UI accessibility foundation.

```bash
# Initialize Shadcn/UI in a new React application
npx shadcn@latest init

# Add individual components
npx shadcn@latest add button
npx shadcn@latest add dialog
npx shadcn@latest add data-table
```

[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#migration-path-for-existing-mui-components]

## Migration Path for Existing MUI Components

If your codebase already contains Material UI components, you are not required to migrate immediately. However, **no new MUI components may be added** — all new component work must use the approved Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS stack.

For teams with existing MUI components requiring a migration path, refer to:

**[PTN-APP-MFE-005 — Design System Migration Pattern](../../patterns/application/micro-frontend/PTN-APP-MFE-005-design-system-migration-pattern.md)**

This pattern defines the approach for replacing existing component library usage with the enterprise design system, including incremental migration strategies that allow existing MUI components to coexist temporarily while new work uses the approved stack.

[decisions/application/ARD-APP-003a-material-ui-rejection-ruling.md#exception-process]

## Exception Process

This ruling enforces [ADR-APP-003](./ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md). This ARD does not grant or deny exceptions — it routes teams to the formal exception process.

**Any team requiring an exception to ADR-APP-003 must:**

1. Submit a formal exception request to the **Architecture Review Board (ARB)** per the ARB process documented in [`governance/processes/architecture-governance.md`](../../governance/processes/architecture-governance.md)
2. Document the specific technical requirement that cannot be met by the approved Shadcn/UI + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS stack
3. Demonstrate that the approved stack has been genuinely assessed and cannot address the requirement
4. Accept the ARB's decision as binding

Exception requests are evaluated by the ARB on the merits of the specific technical requirement. Preference, familiarity, or existing team experience with Material UI are not sufficient grounds for an exception. The ARB will consider whether the requirement can be addressed within the approved stack before granting any exception.
